summary: The 300 s review wall-clock watchdog is never disarmed when a review finishes normally, so it later cancels an already-finished review and emits a false wall_timeout marker.
failure_scenario: A review is admitted (watchdog armed at review.py:326-332), its thread finishes in seconds and _finished records 'finished'. _active[conv] is retained and only join() cancels the watchdog (review.py:484-485), but join() is called only from a later review() for the same conversation, cancel_and_join() or close(). If the conversation goes idle, 300 s later _expire (459-463) sees active.review_id == review_id, prints {"refusal":"wall_timeout"} for a review that completed, sets running.cancelled=True and calls port.cancel(parent, token) -> Hermes cancel_background_review_for_live_turn on the cached parent that will be reused for the next review of that generation. Evidence log claims a timeout that did not happen, and a native cancel is issued against a parent/token that no longer has a live review.
evidence: Synthetic repro using the repo's FakeReviewPort/FakeHermes fixtures (tests/companion/test_review.py): review one window, let it finish (outcome 'finished', active() still returns the id, watchdog armed), then await review._expire(...) as the timer does -> prints '[voice-review] {"refusal":"wall_timeout","version":1}' and port.cancel_calls == 1. Existing test_stale_watchdog_cannot_cancel_successor_review only covers a successor review, not an idle finished one. Native effect of cancelling an idle parent is not verified (Hermes not installed). The call_later lambda also drops the asyncio.create_task reference (can be garbage collected) and close() does not cancel the TimerHandle.

summary: A replayed review request whose earlier run ended 'cancelled' is acknowledged as status 'accepted' without ever being re-run, silently losing the review window.
failure_scenario: Review R for window (conv,gen,seq_from..seq_through) is admitted, then cancelled by cancel_and_join (wall timeout, shutdown, or accept failure path) so the ledger outcome becomes 'cancelled'. Realtime has not seen an ack (or resends after restart) and sends the same range again. _review() finds previous=(id,'cancelled'); only 'reserved'/'unknown' and 'failed' are refused (276-279), everything else falls through to line 280 and returns ReviewAdmission(previous_id,'accepted'). host.py turns that into VoiceReviewAckEvent(status='accepted'), and the realtime sender calls writer.acknowledge_review(request) (voice_review.py:192-193), which retires the window. The cancelled review never completed, no new parent/thread is started, and the window is never reviewed. A 'failed' outcome is correctly refused, so cancelled is inconsistent with the module's own claim that only real accepted dispatch is acknowledged.
evidence: Repro with FakeReviewPort: review(req); cancel_and_join('conv',5) -> outcome 'cancelled'; review(req) again -> status 'accepted', same review_id, port.admissions length still 1 (nothing re-admitted). Realtime-side consequence traced statically through host.py:396-425 and voice_review.py:192; not run end to end.

summary: The browser lease watchdog swallows every expire_if_inactive failure with no evidence and does not guard its own server close.
failure_scenario: expire_if_inactive() raises (e.g. _stop/worker.close failure, or 'session clock regressed' RuntimeError) -> 'except Exception: continue' retries every interval forever with no marker, so an abandoned session that can never be stopped looks identical to a healthy idle one; AGENTS.md requires a bounded [marker] line for a refused bound. Separately, in non-persistent mode 'await self._server.close()' at line 383 is outside the try, so a close failure kills the watchdog task silently (exception only surfaces if close_ingress awaits it), leaving the server up and the lease never enforced again.
evidence: Static read of runtime.py:375-385 and session.py:1852-1878; not run. Retry-on-failure itself is reasonable; the missing evidence and unguarded close are the defect.

summary: A companion that connects but lacks the voice_archive capability emits a marker on every retry instead of once per episode.
failure_scenario: connect() succeeds but link.capabilities lacks VOICE_ARCHIVE_CAPABILITY -> evidence={'refusal':'capability'}, return 'unknown'; _run sleeps backoff (<=30 s) and retries, printing one [voice-archive-send] line per cycle indefinitely (connect failures and transient refusals are explicitly one-per-episode via _unavailable/_transient, this path has no latch). Unbounded log growth for a persistent misconfiguration.
evidence: Static read of voice_archive.py:183-250; compared with _unavailable and _transient latches. Not run.

summary: foreground.py: traced start/cancel/revoke_if_current/settle_revoked/_drain_task/_publish. Revocation is synchronous with no await, stale leases cannot publish (active_lease and active_task identity checked under the state lock), a stuck task intentionally wedges start() with ForegroundTurnDrainTimeout (fail closed), caller cancellation during drain is re-raised after bounded wait. ForegroundTurnLease.invalidate_publications does not stop publish() admission, but its only callers (streaming.py:1074,1130) raise immediately afterward, so no reachable publish follows; not reported.

companion/archive.py + integrity.py + hermes_compat.archive_voice_rows: write-ahead pending/promote protocol, run_to_end thread waiting, lease refresh/fence paths, _guard lock-slot accounting, partition/split_batch/plan_archive (old-generation replay and gap-resend are refused via the expected_pending equality), fingerprint equality binding, NUL/surrogate/timestamp validation. No defect found. hermes_compat memory tail reader, delete/copy capture bounds, and config-signature TOCTOU checks also read without finding a defect.

client/session.py (all 2085 lines read): sequence/replay handling for typed input, approvals and task-proposal decisions, rebind/resync rollback settlement, evidence consent/revoke gates, inactivity expiry. _clear_active_session resets _last_input_request/_last_approval_request so start() not resetting them is not a bug. A post-submit projection.publish capacity failure can leave _last_input_sequence uncommitted, but the worker de-duplicates by typed_sequence (conversation/worker.py:826) and an overflowed projection is already fail-closed, so not reported.
